findings.reason: The protected breadth-first algorithm is clear and optimal, but its app-local surface types the injected tree model as Any and omits the repository-required local equivalent. The sole inert candidate adds the minimal documented TreeNode class and precise TreeNode-or-None annotations while preserving every traversal operation and the solve contract; protected sources remain unchanged.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 314 and its Python verticalOrder surface. The Reference preserves left-to-right columns, top-to-bottom order, same-position left-to-right ties, all three source examples, both constraints, and three accessible diagrams equivalent to the source images.

The immutable Any-annotated native source remains tied to verified submission 2064372913 and structurally aligned with the protected app-local helper. The candidate changes only the app-local model declaration and annotations; coordinate assignment, left-before-right BFS, bucket order, bounds, and result construction are identical.

The former 192-node performance tier exceeded the documented 100-node maximum. The rebuilt legal 16, 48, and 96-node left chains span 6x and create one column per node. The candidate passes all nine executions at -0.00 relative growth and 0.98x; a correct per-column tree rescan passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.37 and 50.55x.

The Approach now records the candidate's local TreeNode model and otherwise exactly derives horizontal coordinates, contiguous column bounds, BFS depth and tie ordering, final bucket order, and linear traversal and storage bounds.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, including all three source examples, both constraints, tie ordering, and independently authored diagrams preserving all three source trees and vertical groups.

coverage: All three authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact level-order trees and vertical columns; the formerly missing deep-tie example is restored.
The legal empty tree is now a trial rather than an invented source sample, and the formerly hidden perfect-tree tie case is visible.
Empty, single-node, and exact 100-node trees cover the full node-count boundary, while a same-position tie uses values -100 and 100 to cover both value endpoints.
Left- and right-skewed chains verify left-to-right column enumeration, while sparse, perfect, and deep trees verify top-to-bottom ordering and repeated columns.
A deliberately reverse-valued same-row same-column tie verifies left-to-right BFS order rather than numeric sorting.

An independent sorted (column, row, breadth-first order) record oracle verified all 10 authored results and all three benchmark results; the candidate also matched it on 11,497 exhaustive ordered trees with zero through five nodes labeled from {-1, 0, 1}.
All 10 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 16-, 48-, and 96-node left-chain workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
